P6h: One key to this whole thing is that cooperation shouldn't quietly turn into merging. The FEC has full members and communities working toward full membership, and Friends who may just want to stay friends. Also, people need a practical freedom to move between communities, and that takes work: housing, status, health coverage, records, labor accounting, travel costs, taxes, and disputes over the transition all have to be set up, or the freedom to move is just decorative. Fortunately, that interface can often be thin, saying who's responsible for what while somebody crosses between them, and communities don't have to have the same internal systems for it to work.
